title: The receipt decoder takes the first WETH Withdrawal (or WETH Transfer to the wallet) anywhere in the sell receipt without checking who emitted it, so a token whose transfer hook moves WETH can make the recorded sell proceeds wrong

evidence.note: first Withdrawal log from the WETH address wins; its src (the account that unwrapped) is not compared to the router
fallback: first WETH Transfer with to == wallet; from is not compared to the pool
receipt.status is not read (safe today: both callers decode only hashes already proven included with status 1)
the decoded amountOut is written to the sell trade row; realized P&L and the dashboard daily loss read from trades (api/routes/risk.ts:90, health.ts:64-66)

sibling_sites_checked: Both callers: exitEngine.ts:1059 (full sell) and :1546 (partial sell), each after a confirmed hash (private landed / guard included / public wait() that throws on status 0). Whether the risk manager's daily-loss limit (riskManager.ts, BUY/DB slice) reads amount_out was not traced here; that is why the entry is a candidate.
severity_rationale: S3: needs an adversarial token (a transfer hook that unwraps or sends WETH during the sell); the effect is wrong bookkeeping (sell proceeds, P&L, possibly a loss limit computed from them), not a direct loss.
recommendation: Phase 29: match the Withdrawal whose src is the router used (V2) or the Transfer whose from is the pool (V3), or compute proceeds from the wallet balance delta; trace whether any limit is computed from amount_out.
